extracted.intended_audience: Users of the PARI/GP library: mathematicians, computational number theorists, and developers using PARI/GP
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for PARI/GP library functions in the algebra / polynomials & power series sections; describes function purpose, arguments, return values, algorithmic notes, and usage warnings/examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: algsplittingdata
rubrics_metrics.description: Given an algebra A (from alginit), returns splitting data [t,Lb,Lbi] describing a splitting of A relative to its center.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example usage shown; library syntax: GEN algsplittingdata(GEN al). Returned objects include a vector t and matrices Lb, Lbi. No further caveats in this chunk.

rubrics_metrics.name: algsplittingfield
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a central simple algebra al output by alginit, returns an rnf structure: the splitting field of al stored in al, as a relative extension of the center.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: algsplittingfield(A).pol returned x^2 - y in example. Library syntax: GEN algsplittingfield(GEN al).

rubrics_metrics.name: algsplittingmatrix
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a central simple algebra al (from alginit) that contains data describing an isomorphism φ : A ⊗K L → Md(L), returns the matrix φ(x).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accepts matrices with coefficients in al. Example shows returned matrix entries as Mod(...) elements. Library syntax: GEN algsplittingmatrix(GEN al, GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: algsqr
rubrics_metrics.description: Given an element x in al, computes its square x^2 in the algebra al.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also accepts a square matrix with coefficients in al. Example: algsqr(A,[1,0,2,0]~) returns vector of coordinates. Library syntax: GEN algsqr(GEN al, GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: algsub
rubrics_metrics.description: Given two elements x and y in al, computes their difference x - y in the algebra al.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also accepts matrices with coefficients in al. Library syntax: GEN algsub(GEN al, GEN x, GEN y).

rubrics_metrics.name: algsubalg
rubrics_metrics.description: Given al (table algebra from algtableinit) and B being a basis of a subalgebra represented by a matrix, returns an algebra isomorphic to B.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example constructs table algebra and extracts subalgebra; library syntax: GEN algsubalg(GEN al, GEN B).

rubrics_metrics.name: algtableinit
rubrics_metrics.description: Initialize the associative (table) algebra over K = Q (p omitted) or Fp defined by the multiplication table mt. The algebra is given as a t_VEC of n matrices giving left multiplication by basis elements; assumes e1 = 1 and integrality for K = Q.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: input finite dimensional K-algebra to compute its radical and split quotient. The PARI object stores characteristic, multiplication table, and traces. Example: upper triangular 2x2 matrices. Library syntax: GEN algtableinit(GEN mt, GEN p = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: algtensor
rubrics_metrics.description: Given two algebras al1 and al2, computes their tensor product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For table algebras output by algtableinit, the flag maxord is ignored. For central simple algebras output by alginit, computes a maximal order by default; set maxord=0 to prevent this computation. Currently only implemented for cyclic algebras of coprime degree over the same center K; tensor product is over K. Library syntax: GEN algtensor(GEN al1, GEN al2, long maxord).

rubrics_metrics.name: algtrace
rubrics_metrics.description: Given an element x in al, computes its trace. If al is a table algebra (algtableinit) returns absolute trace in Fp or Q; if al is output of alginit returns the reduced trace in the center.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also accepts a square matrix with coefficients in al. Example: algtrace(A,[5,0,0,1]~) = 11. Library syntax: GEN algtrace(GEN al, GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: algtype
rubrics_metrics.description: Given an algebra al (from alginit or algtableinit), returns an integer indicating the type of algebra: 0 not a valid algebra; 1 table algebra (algtableinit); 2 central simple algebra represented by multiplication table over its center; 3 central simple algebra represented as a cyclic algebra.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show return values for various initializations. Library syntax: long algtype(GEN al).

rubrics_metrics.name: O(p^e) / zeropadic / zeroser
rubrics_metrics.description: Constructs a p-adic 0 of precision e for integer p>2; in other cases returns a power series zero with precision given by ev where v is X-adic valuation of p relative to main variable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN ggrando() / GEN zeropadic(GEN p, long e) for p-adic and GEN zeroser(long v, long e) for a power series zero in variable v.

rubrics_metrics.name: bezoutres (alias)
rubrics_metrics.description: Deprecated alias for polresultantext.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN polresultantext0(GEN A, GEN B, long v = -1) where v is a variable number.

rubrics_metrics.name: deriv
rubrics_metrics.description: Derivative of x with respect to main variable (or v if given). Derivative of scalar type is zero; derivative of vector/matrix is componentwise. For t_POLMOD main variable is determined among coefficient polynomials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shortcut: x' denotes derivative wrt main variable. Library syntax: GEN deriv(GEN x, long v = -1).

rubrics_metrics.name: diffop
rubrics_metrics.description: Let v be a vector of variables and d a vector of same length; returns the image of x by the n-power (n default 1) of the differential operator D that takes value d[i] on v[i]. Applies componentwise; when applied to t_POLMOD, missing modulus variable value is derived using the implicit function theorem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: diffop(E*X,[X,E],[1,2*X*E]) and differentiation with relations (Sin^2+Cos^2=1). Can compute Bell polynomials via Faa di Bruno. Library syntax: GEN diffop0(GEN x, GEN v, GEN d, long n) or GEN diffop(GEN x, GEN v, GEN d) for n=1.

rubrics_metrics.name: eval / geval
rubrics_metrics.description: Replaces formal variables in x by values assigned after creation; in GP eval(x) executes string x as a GP command. Mainly useful in GP, not library mode.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If x is a string, eval(x) executes it. Syntax errors raise e_SYNTAX exceptions which can be trapped with iferr. Library syntax: GEN geval(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: factorpadic
rubrics_metrics.description: p-adic factorization of polynomial pol to precision r; result is two-column matrix like factor. This is not factorization over Z/prZ but approximations in Q/prZ of true factorization in Qp[X].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factors are normalized so leading coefficient is a power of p. Method: modified round 4 algorithm of Zassenhaus. If pol has inexact t_PADIC coefficients, polynomial is first made integral then lifted; advise to only factor polynomials with exact rational coefficients to avoid pitfalls. Library syntax: factorpadic(GEN f,GEN p, long r).

rubrics_metrics.name: intformal (integ)
rubrics_metrics.description: Formal integration of x with respect to main variable (or v). Since PARI cannot represent logarithmic or arctangent terms, any such term in the result yields an error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argument x can be any type. When x is rational function, base ring assumed integral domain characteristic zero. For t_POLMOD main variable defined among coefficients; integrating with respect to modulus' main variable is meaningless and yields an error. Library syntax: GEN integ(GEN x, long v = -1).

rubrics_metrics.name: padicappr / Zp_appr
rubrics_metrics.description: Vector of p-adic roots of polynomial pol congruent to p-adic number a modulo p, with same p-adic precision as a. a can be t_PADIC or an integral element of finite extension (t_POLMOD).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a is an element of a finite extension, result is vector of roots in same extension. Library syntax: GEN padicappr(GEN pol, GEN a). Also GEN Zp_appr(GEN f, GEN a) when a is t_PADIC.

rubrics_metrics.name: padicfields
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns a vector of polynomials generating all extensions of degree N of Qp; N may be [n,d] to return extensions of degree n and discriminant p^d. The list is minimal (non-isomorphic extensions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If flag=1 return [P,e,f,d,c] with ramification index e, residual degree f, valuation of discriminant d, and number of conjugate fields c. If flag=2 return only number of extensions via Krasner's formula. Each returned polynomial P has a root α = uniformizer + generator of residue field so powers of α generate ring of p-adic integers. Library syntax: GEN padicfields0(GEN p, GEN N, long flag) and variants.

rubrics_metrics.name: polchebyshev
rubrics_metrics.description: Return nth Chebyshev polynomial of first kind Tn (flag=1) or second kind Un (flag=2), evaluated at a (x by default).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Polynomials satisfy 3-term relation P_{n+1} = 2x P_n - P_{n-1}; initial conditions given. For n<0 definitions given (Tn = T_{-n}). Library syntax: GEN polchebyshev_eval(long n, long flag, GEN a = NULL). Variants available for returning polynomial in a variable.

rubrics_metrics.name: polclass
rubrics_metrics.description: Return a polynomial in Z[x] generating the Hilbert class field for imaginary quadratic discriminant D. If inv=0 use modular j-function to return classical Hilbert polynomial; otherwise use specified class invariant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many invariants supported (Weber f, double eta quotients w_{p,q}, γ2=j^{1/3}, etc.) but only under technical congruence/ramification conditions listed (examples enumerated: inv values 0,1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9,10,14,15,21,23,24,26,27,28,35,39 with various D congruence constraints). Algorithm uses Chinese remainder approach modulo small primes (not floating-point evaluation), so class invariant chosen may be any root of modular polynomial and precise assertions about which root cannot be made. Examples: polclass(-163) returns x + 262537412640768000. Library syntax: GEN polclass(GEN D, long inv, long x = -1).

rubrics_metrics.name: polcoeff
rubrics_metrics.description: Coefficient of degree n of polynomial x with respect to main variable (or v). If n greater than degree result is zero. Applies to scalars, rational functions with monomial denominator, power series (valuation behavior), vectors/matrices componentwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If n greater than largest significant degree on power series an error is issued. Library syntax: GEN polcoeff0(GEN x, long n, long v = -1).

rubrics_metrics.name: polcyclo
rubrics_metrics.description: Return n-th cyclotomic polynomial (Φ_n) or evaluate it at a (a default 'x'). Integer n must be positive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Algorithm: reduce to squarefree n, use Φ_{np}(x) = Φ_n(x^p)/Φ_n(x); evaluated case uses product formula ∏_{d|n} (x^d - 1)^{μ(n/d)}. In evaluated case algorithm assumes a^d - 1 either 0 or invertible for all d|n; if base ring has zero divisors use subst(polcyclo(n),x,a). Library syntax: GEN polcyclo_eval(long n, GEN a = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: polcyclofactors
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns a vector of polynomials whose product is the product of distinct cyclotomic polynomials dividing f.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In general output polynomials are products of cyclotomic polynomials and not necessarily irreducible. Example and usage with poliscycloprod and poliscyclo illustrated. Library syntax: GEN polcyclofactors(GEN f).

rubrics_metrics.name: poldegree
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree of polynomial x in main variable (or v). Degree of 0 is -oo; degree of non-zero scalar is 0; for non-zero polynomial/rational function returns ordinary degree. Raises an error otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN gppoldegree(GEN x, long v = -1). Also long poldegree(GEN x, long v) variant returning -LONG_MAX for x=0.

rubrics_metrics.name: poldisc
rubrics_metrics.description: Discriminant of polynomial pol in main variable (or v). Uses modular algorithm over Z or Q, subresultant algorithm otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to t_QUAD and t_QFI/t_QFR types for convenience. Examples given. Library syntax: GEN poldisc0(GEN pol, long v = -1).

rubrics_metrics.name: poldiscreduced (reduced discriminant vector)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reduced discriminant vector of an integral, monic polynomial f: vector of elementary divisors of Z[α]/f(α)Z[α] where α is root of f. Components positive and product equals absolute value of discriminant of f.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax (implementation name): GEN reduceddiscsmith(GEN f).

rubrics_metrics.name: polgraeffe
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns the Graeffe transform g of f such that g(x^2) = f(x) f(-x).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN polgraeffe(GEN f).

rubrics_metrics.name: polhensellift
rubrics_metrics.description: Given prime p, integral polynomial A with leading coefficient a p-unit, vector B of integral polynomials monic and pairwise relatively prime mod p whose product ≡ A/lc(A) mod p, lifts B to polynomials whose product ≡ A mod p^e.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: More generally can lift factorization over Fp[t]/(T) by replacing p with [p,T]; example given lifting in Zp[t]/(T,p^6). Library syntax: GEN polhensellift(GEN A, GEN B, GEN p, long e).

rubrics_metrics.name: polhermite
rubrics_metrics.description: nth Hermite polynomial H_n evaluated at a (x by default), defined by Hn(x) = (-1)^n e^{x^2} d^n/dx^n e^{-x^2}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN polhermite_eval(long n, GEN a = NULL). Variant GEN polhermite(long n, long v) returns polynomial in variable v.

rubrics_metrics.name: polinterpolate
rubrics_metrics.description: Given data vectors X and Y of same length n, finds interpolating polynomial P of minimal degree passing through points and evaluates it at t; if Y omitted interpolates (i, X[i]). If present, &e will contain an error estimate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN polint(GEN X, GEN Y = NULL, GEN t = NULL, GEN *e = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: poliscyclo
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns 0 if f is not cyclotomic polynomial, otherwise returns n>0 if f = Φ_n (n-th cyclotomic polynomial).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example usage: poliscyclo(x^4-x^2+1) = 12. Library syntax: long poliscyclo(GEN f).

rubrics_metrics.name: poliscycloprod
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns 1 if f is a product of cyclotomic polynomials, 0 otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful combined with factor to identify cyclotomic factors. Library syntax: long poliscycloprod(GEN f).

rubrics_metrics.name: polisirreducible
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns 1 if pol (univariate in current version) is non-constant and irreducible, 0 otherwise. Irreducibility checked over the smallest base field over which pol seems defined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: long isirreducible(GEN pol).

rubrics_metrics.name: pollead
rubrics_metrics.description: Leading coefficient of polynomial or power series x with respect to main variable (or v).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN pollead(GEN x, long v = -1).

rubrics_metrics.name: pollegendre
rubrics_metrics.description: nth Legendre polynomial evaluated at a (x by default).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN pollegendre_eval(long n, GEN a = NULL). Variant GEN pollegendre(long n, long v) returns polynomial in variable v.

rubrics_metrics.name: polmodular
rubrics_metrics.description: Return the modular polynomial of prime level L in variables x and y for the modular function specified by inv (0 default = j, 1 = Weber-f, 5 = γ2 = j^{1/3}, etc.). If x is in finite field returns modular polynomial evaluated at j; if derivs non-zero and j in finite field, returns triple with polynomial and its first and second derivatives evaluated at j.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: polmodular(3) returns full polynomial; polmodular(7,1,, 'J) returned a simple form. Library syntax: GEN polmodular(long L, long inv, GEN x = NULL, long y = -1, long derivs).

rubrics_metrics.name: polrecip
rubrics_metrics.description: Reciprocal polynomial of pol (coefficients reversed). pol must be a polynomial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN polrecip(GEN pol).

rubrics_metrics.name: polresultant
rubrics_metrics.description: Resultant of two polynomials x and y with exact entries, with respect to main variables (or v). If you need u,v such that x*u + y*v = Res(x,y) use polresultantext.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If flag=0 (default) uses best algorithm (subresultant, modular, or Sylvester determinant depending on inputs). If flag=1 forces Sylvester determinant (usually slower). Library syntax: GEN polresultant0(GEN x, GEN y, long v = -1, long flag).

rubrics_metrics.name: polresultantext
rubrics_metrics.description: Find polynomials U and V such that A*U + B*V = R where R is resultant of A and B; returns [U,V,R]. Algorithm uses subresultant and assumes base ring is a domain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show how to compute U,V,R and verify identity. Library syntax: GEN polresultantext0(GEN A, GEN B, long v = -1).

rubrics_metrics.name: polroots
rubrics_metrics.description: Complex roots of polynomial T as column vector, each root repeated according to multiplicity. Precision is determined by realprecision in GP and must be explicit in library mode.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Algorithm is modification of Sch¨onhage’s root-finding algorithm (Gourdon). Guaranteed to converge; for rational coefficients roots guaranteed to required relative accuracy. Library syntax: GEN roots(GEN T, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: polrootsmod
rubrics_metrics.description: Row vector of roots modulo p of polynomial pol. Multiple roots not repeated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If p very small flag=1 uses naive search. Library syntax: GEN rootmod0(GEN pol, GEN p, long flag).

rubrics_metrics.name: polrootspadic
rubrics_metrics.description: Vector of p-adic roots of polynomial pol given to p-adic precision r (p prime). Multiple roots not repeated. These are approximations in Z/p^rZ of true roots in Qp, not roots in Z/p^rZ ring structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If pol has inexact t_PADIC coefficients, polynomial is made integral then lifted, so results approximate roots of an exact polynomial p-adically close to input; advisable to factor only polynomials with exact rational coefficients. Library syntax: GEN rootpadic(GEN x, GEN p, long r).

rubrics_metrics.name: polrootsreal
rubrics_metrics.description: Real roots of polynomial T with rational coefficients, multiple roots included per multiplicity, given to relative accuracy realprecision. If ab is provided [a,b] restrict to that closed interval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Algorithm: modification of Uspensky’s method (Descartes' rule) following Rouillier & Zimmerman; guaranteed to converge for exact inputs. Remark: if T = Q(x^h) and ab omitted routine applies to Q and then takes h-th roots; if ab is provided user should transform themselves. Library syntax: GEN realroots(GEN T, GEN ab = NULL, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: polsturm
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of real roots of the real squarefree polynomial T. If ab present count roots in interval [a,b].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer exact inputs (no t_REAL) so result is guaranteed and fast algorithm (Uspensky) used; otherwise Sturm's algorithm used and may be wrong due to round-off. Not squarefree inputs raise domain error. Examples illustrate precision errors when input is inexact. Library syntax: long RgX_sturmpart(GEN T, GEN ab) or long sturm(GEN T) for ab=NULL.

rubrics_metrics.name: polsubcyclo
rubrics_metrics.description: Gives polynomials (in variable v) defining sub-Abelian extensions of degree d of cyclotomic field Q(ζ_n), where d | φ(n).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If exactly one such extension output is a polynomial, else a vector of polynomials possibly empty. To force vector output use concat([], polsubcyclo(n,d)). galoissubcyclo allows specifying which sub-extension. Library syntax: GEN polsubcyclo(long n, long d, long v = -1).

rubrics_metrics.name: polsylvestermatrix
rubrics_metrics.description: Forms Sylvester matrix corresponding to two polynomials x and y, with coefficients put in columns (natural direction for solving equations afterwards).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful when dealing with polynomials with inexact entries because polynomial Euclidean division is less meaningful there. Library syntax: GEN sylvestermatrix(GEN x, GEN y).

rubrics_metrics.name: polsym
rubrics_metrics.description: Creates column vector of symmetric powers of the roots of polynomial x up to power n, using Newton's formula.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN polsym(GEN x, long n).

rubrics_metrics.name: poltchebi (alias)
rubrics_metrics.description: Deprecated alias for polchebyshev.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN polchebyshev1(long n, long v = -1).

rubrics_metrics.name: polzagier
rubrics_metrics.description: Creates Zagier’s polynomial P_n^{(m)} used in functions sumalt and sumpos (with flag=1) for convergence acceleration of alternating series.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition and special cases provided; library syntax: GEN polzag(long n, long m).

rubrics_metrics.name: serconvol
rubrics_metrics.description: Convolution (Hadamard product) of two power series x and y: if x = ∑ a_k X^k and y = ∑ b_k X^k then serconvol(x,y) = ∑ a_k b_k X^k.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN convol(GEN x, GEN y).

rubrics_metrics.name: serlaplace
rubrics_metrics.description: If x is power series with non-negative exponents or polynomial and x = ∑ (a_k/k!) X^k then serlaplace(x) = ∑ a_k X^k (formal Laplace transform on series).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN laplace(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: serreverse
rubrics_metrics.description: Reverse power series: given s with valuation exactly 1 returns t such that t(s) = x. s must have valuation 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: serreverse(tan(x)) returns series inverse of tan up to given precision. Library syntax: GEN serreverse(GEN s).

rubrics_metrics.name: subst
rubrics_metrics.description: Replace simple variable y by argument z in polynomial-like expression x. Substitution applied componentwise to vectors/matrices/lists. If x is not a genuine polynomial substitution treats scalar components as degree 0 polynomials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beware substitution by non-square matrices is forbidden. If x is power series z must be polynomial, power series, or rational function. Use substvec for several simultaneous substitutions and substpol to replace polynomial expressions. Library syntax: GEN gsubst(GEN x, long y, GEN z).

rubrics_metrics.name: substpol
rubrics_metrics.description: Replace polynomial 'variable' y by argument z in polynomial-like expression x; y is allowed to be any polynomial (not only a simple variable). Substitution is done by moding components recursively by y - t where t is new free variable then substituting t by z.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show nontrivial behavior when y is polynomial different from simple variable. Library syntax: GEN gsubstpol(GEN x, GEN y, GEN z). Function gdeflate also attempts writing T(x) as t(x^d) and returns NULL if it fails.

rubrics_metrics.name: substvec
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform simultaneous substitutions: v is vector of monomials (variables) and w vector of expressions; replace occurrences of v_i by w_i simultaneously.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substitutions done simultaneously by temporary variables to avoid cascading replacements. Examples given. Library syntax: GEN gsubstvec(GEN x, GEN v, GEN w).

rubrics_metrics.name: sumformal
rubrics_metrics.description: Formal sum of polynomial expression f with respect to main variable v (or main variable if omitted); returns polynomial F vanishing at 0 such that F(b)-F(a) = sum_{v=a+1}^b f(v).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: sumformal(n) gives 1/2*n^2+1/2*n; can be used to produce closed forms for sums. Library syntax: GEN sumformal(GEN f, long v = -1).

rubrics_metrics.name: taylor
rubrics_metrics.description: Taylor expansion around 0 of x with respect to simple variable t to order d (default seriesprecision). x may be many types (rational function etc.). Unlike Ser which respects valuation, taylor adds O(t^d) to all components of x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: taylor(x/(1+y), y, 5) returns polynomial with O(y^5) term. Library syntax: (implied) taylor(x,t,d).
